A single-celled organism lives in freshwater. Water that enters the cytoplasm of the cell by osmosis is collected into a structure called the contractile vacuole. To remove the water the contractile vacuole fuses with the cell surface membrane.

options.A: The water potential gradient between the cell and the solution increased, causing water to move into the cell more rapidly and the contractile vacuole to empty more frequently.
options.B: The water potential gradient between the cell and the solution increased, causing water to move into the cell less rapidly and the contractile vacuole to empty less frequently.
options.C: The water potential gradient between the cell and the solution decreased, causing water to move into the cell more rapidly and the contractile vacuole to empty more frequently.
options.D: The water potential gradient between the cell and the solution decreased, causing water to move into the cell less rapidly and the contractile vacuole to empty less frequently.
